metadata.title: Does ICT involvement really matter? An investigation of Turkey’s case in PISA 2018

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses the Turkish dataset from PISA 2018 and applies PISA’s complex sampling design, where schools are sampled first and students second, producing a layered (nested) structure. To reduce standard errors under this design, the authors state that sampling weights are employed and that PISA uses balanced repeated replication (BRR) with Fay’s variant using 80 replications. Analyses were conducted with the OECD International Database Analyzer (IDB Analyzer), which applies the appropriate survey design and replicate-weight framework for PISA estimates. The paper does not report a specific single weight variable name (e.g., W_FSTUWT), but the use of IDB Analyzer with BRR implies design-weighted estimation for the regression models using plausible values.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the Turkish dataset from the 2018 PISA event, restricting to students with math and science test scores and responses to the ICT Familiarity Questionnaire. Excluded ICT Familiarity Questionnaire respondents who indicated they had not previously used a digital device (IC002 scale; n=167), leaving 6,723 cases. Performed missing value analyses and excluded cases with missing data via listwise deletion because construct-level missingness did not exceed 5%, yielding a final analytic sample of 6,101 cases.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Two-step hierarchical regression (IDB Analyzer with PVs). Step 1 R²=0.11; Step 2 R²=0.20. Significant predictors in Step 2: ESCS β=0.34 (p<0.001); ICTHOME β=-0.10 (p<0.001); ICTCLASS β=0.18 (p<0.001); USESCH β=-0.15 (p<0.001); HOMESCH β=-0.07 (p<0.001); ENTUSE β=0.08 (p<0.001); ICTOUTSIDE β=-0.05 (p<0.01); COMPICT β=0.11 (p<0.001); INTICT β=0.05 (p<0.001); SOIAICT β=-0.09 (p<0.001); AUTICT not significant (β=0.02).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 (Turkey) the study leveraged socioeconomic status (ESCS), ICT availability (ICTHOME), ICT use (ICTCLASS, USESCH, HOMESCH, ENTUSE, ICTOUTSIDE), and ICT attitude (COMPICT, INTICT, SOIAICT, AUTICT) to predict math achievement (PVs), finding that ESCS positively predicted achievement while ICTHOME negatively predicted achievement and subject-related ICT use in lessons (ICTCLASS) positively predicted achievement. This indicates that ICT’s relationship with achievement depends on how it is used and students’ ICT competence, suggesting that policy should avoid assuming that more ICT access or generic ICT use will improve math outcomes.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Two-step hierarchical regression (IDB Analyzer with PVs). Step 1 R²=0.11; Step 2 R²=0.21. Significant predictors in Step 2: ESCS β=0.32 (p<0.001); ICTHOME β=-0.09 (p<0.001); ICTCLASS β=0.20 (p<0.001); USESCH β=-0.17 (p<0.001); HOMESCH β=-0.07 (p<0.001); ENTUSE β=0.08 (p<0.001); ICTOUTSIDE β=-0.04 (p<0.05); COMPICT β=0.13 (p<0.001); INTICT β=0.06 (p<0.001); AUTICT β=0.04 (p<0.05); SOIAICT β=-0.11 (p<0.001).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 (Turkey) the study leveraged socioeconomic status (ESCS), ICT availability (ICTHOME), ICT use (ICTCLASS, USESCH, HOMESCH, ENTUSE, ICTOUTSIDE), and ICT attitude (COMPICT, INTICT, AUTICT, SOIAICT) to predict science achievement (PVs), finding that ESCS positively predicted achievement while ICTHOME negatively predicted achievement and subject-related ICT use in lessons (ICTCLASS) positively predicted achievement. This indicates that ICT can be beneficial when integrated into structured, subject-specific instruction and when students feel competent, but that broader or socially oriented ICT use may be associated with lower science performance.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes the Turkish dataset from PISA 2018, focusing on math and science achievement estimated via plausible values (PV1MATH–PV10MATH and PV1SCIE–PV10SCIE) and ICT Familiarity Questionnaire indices. The analytic sample was 6,101 students after excluding non-digital-device users and applying listwise deletion for missing data. Using two-step hierarchical regression in IDB Analyzer (with BRR/Fay replicate weights), the models explained modest variance: math R² increased from 0.11 to 0.20, and science R² increased from 0.11 to 0.21 after adding ICT constructs. ESCS was a consistent positive predictor, while ICT availability at home (ICTHOME) was significantly negative. Among ICT use variables, subject-related ICT use during lessons (ICTCLASS) and leisure ICT use (ENTUSE) were positive, whereas general school ICT use (USESCH) and schoolwork-related outside use (HOMESCH) were negative; ICT competence and interest were positive, while ICT use for social communication (SOIAICT) was negative. The authors caution against causal interpretation because the design is relational and based on self-reported ICT measures.
